package_info.why_malicious: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2022-24828) in Composer allowed attackers to gain remote code execution on Packagist.org, enabling them to hijack package metadata and force users to download malicious dependencies, potentially compromising millions of PHP projects and servers.

execution_context.file_location: Packagist server-side logic (not a specific file in user packages, but in the repository infrastructure)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Remote code execution via crafted package metadata or dependency resolution logic (exact exploit code not disclosed in the report).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user installs or updates a package, the compromised Packagist server could serve malicious package metadata, causing Composer to download and execute attacker-controlled code, leading to arbitrary code execution on the user's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote code execution on a central package repository enables attackers to inject arbitrary code into any downstream project using Composer.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior expects package repositories to serve only legitimate, verified package metadata and code. Here, the repository could be manipulated to serve malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be serving updated or patched packages, but never arbitrary code execution or metadata tampering.
key_indicators: Remote code execution on package repository
Manipulation of package metadata to redirect downloads

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits vulnerability in Packagist to gain remote code execution on the repository server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to manipulate package metadata and serve malicious dependencies.

attack_chain.action: Compromised Packagist serves malicious package metadata or binaries to Composer clients during install/update.
attack_chain.leads_to: Downstream users unknowingly install backdoored or malicious packages.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes on user servers, potentially exfiltrating data, modifying configurations, or establishing persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Widespread compromise of PHP applications and infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected changes in package metadata or download URLs from Packagist
Composer installing packages from non-standard or previously unseen sources
Sudden appearance of new or modified dependencies during install/update
file_indicators: Unexpected or unauthorized files appearing in vendor/ directories
Modified composer.lock or composer.json with suspicious package sources
network_indicators: Composer client making requests to unfamiliar or attacker-controlled domains
Unusual outbound connections during or after package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Composer install/update operations for unexpected changes in package sources or metadata. Alert on downloads from non-standard domains or sudden changes in dependency trees. Use file integrity monitoring on composer.json and composer.lock. Correlate with network logs to detect outbound connections to suspicious domains during package installation. Regularly audit SBOMs and verify package signatures where possible.
